pages.summary: A model of partial differential equations in two dimensions, its coefficients and boundary conditions, and its solution by finite elements.
body: `createpde` makes a model of N equations m*u'' + d*u' - div(c*grad(u)) + a*u = f (one unless N is given). It is built up in steps: a geometry (`geometryFromEdges`), a mesh (`generateMesh`), the coefficients (`specifyCoefficients`, all five, 0 for a term not there, numbers or functions of location and state), conditions on the boundary's edges (`applyBoundaryCondition`: Dirichlet, u given; Neumann, n.(c*grad(u)) + q*u = g given; or mixed), and initial conditions for a problem in time. `solvepde` then solves it: stationary when m and d are zero, else at the times asked for. An edge with no condition is insulated (g = q = 0); the last condition given on an edge holds.
syntax: specifyCoefficients(model, 'm', m, 'd', d, 'c', c, 'a', a, 'f', f)

A bar held at both ends, then with a flux at one

pages.summary: A geometry made of shapes, given to a model, and drawn.
body: `decsg` combines circles, polygons, rectangles and ellipses (a column of the geometry matrix each) by a set formula of their names: + for union, * for intersection, - for difference. It gives the edges of the regions that result, a column each, with the faces on their left and right. `geometryFromEdges` makes that the model's geometry (or takes a geometry function). `pdegplot` draws it, with the labels of its edges, faces and vertices when asked: the numbers that boundary conditions and coefficients refer to.
syntax: Combined by a formula of their names.

examples.title: A plate with a hole

pages.summary: A triangular mesh of a model's geometry, drawn, and in the point, edge and triangle form.
body: `generateMesh` covers the geometry with triangles about Hmax across (a tenth of the geometry's size unless given), quadratic ones by default, with a node at the middle of each side, curved along curved edges; `'GeometricOrder', 'linear'` makes plain triangles. The mesh is stored in the model and returned: Nodes (2-by-n) and Elements (a column each). `pdemesh` draws it, with node or element numbers when asked. `meshToPet` gives it as p (the nodes), e (the boundary's pieces with their edges) and t (the elements' corners and their face).

examples.title: Coarse and fine

pages.summary: The nodes and elements of a mesh in a region: on an edge or a face, in a box or a circle, or nearest to points.
body: Both give a row of numbers, to pick out a solution's values or the elements of a part. `findNodes` takes the nodes on edges or faces (`'region'`), within a box or a circle, or the node nearest each point. `findElements` takes the elements of faces, those with all their nodes within a box or a circle, or those attached to nodes.

examples.title: An edge, a point, a disc

pages.summary: Initial values for a problem in time, or a starting guess for a nonlinear one.
body: The initial value is a number (one for each equation), a vector of nodal values, a function of location (location.x, location.y), or the last solution of earlier results; with m not zero, a second argument gives the initial rate. Given on faces, it holds there only.

examples.title: Heat leaving a square

pages.summary: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a model: its modes.
body: The lambda in the range [lo, hi] (hi may be Inf) for which -div(c*grad(u)) + a*u = lambda*d*u has a solution with the model's boundary conditions (Dirichlet ones taken as zero): the vibration modes of a membrane, or the decay rates of heat. Eigenvalues come in order, Eigenvectors a column each at the nodes.

examples.title: The modes of a square membrane

pages.summary: The finite-element matrices of a model, to solve or study by hand.
body: K comes from c, A from a, F from f, Q and G from the Neumann conditions' q and g, M from m (or d), and H and R state the Dirichlet conditions as H*u = R. All are sparse, with the components of a system one after another.

pages.summary: A PDE solution, and its gradient, at any points.
body: Both evaluate the elements' basis functions at the points (given as x and y, or as a matrix with a column for each point), NaN outside the mesh. For a system, iU picks the components; for a solution in time or a set of modes, iT picks the times or modes, a column each.
syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, iU, iT)

pages.summary: A PDE solution drawn over its mesh: in colour, as contours, as a surface, with arrows.
body: The nodal values fill the elements in interpolated colour (a quadratic element as four triangles); `'ZData'` lifts them into a surface, `'Contour', 'on'` adds contour lines, `'Mesh', 'on'` the elements' sides, and `'FlowData'` arrows of a vector field such as the gradient. Given only a model or a mesh, it draws the mesh.
